headline: A law that lets the State Department offer cash rewards for tips leading to the arrest or transfer of foreign nationals accused of war crimes under a wider set of legal definitions.
what_it_does: The law expands the State Department's existing rewards program. Before, rewards could be offered only when the accused person's crimes were defined under the statutes of an international criminal tribunal. Now rewards can also cover crimes as defined under the law of the country where they occurred or under U.S. law.

who_it_affects.group: People who have information about foreign nationals accused of war crimes, crimes against humanity, or genocide
who_it_affects.how: They may be eligible for a State Department reward if their information leads to an arrest, conviction, or transfer of the accused person.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign nationals accused of war crimes, crimes against humanity, or genocide
who_it_affects.how: They can now be the subject of a reward offer under a broader set of legal definitions of these crimes.
It has broader authority to set up and pay rewards for information about these accused individuals.

when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not give a separate start date, so the law appears to have taken effect when it was signed on December 27, 2022.
